Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: You have earned the truth. I have been keeping more from you than I should.
Suggested line: You have earned the truth, so here is the first piece of it: I am not only a tortoise who bakes.
Why: Restores Maren's own turn into the confession; the current line says she is hiding things instead of showing it.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: I wasn't sure I could trust you before. I am now.
Suggested line: I wasn't sure of you before. I am sure now. Mostly.
Why: Restores her sting in the tail; 'Mostly.' is pure Maren and keeps her guarded at stage 2.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: I have been hiding here ever since.
Suggested line: I have been hiding here ever since, with my hands in pie dough, where nobody would ask what else they had made.
Why: Gives the bare line a concrete, sincere image: the pie was where she hid the hands that blew the glass.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: One Path left under {villain}'s thumb. The whole town is holding its breath. It's murder on my knees.
Suggested line: One Path left under {villain}'s thumb. The whole town is holding its breath. I can hold mine for a week. They cannot.
Why: The knees joke does not follow from holding breath; a tortoise who can hold hers all week does.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You find a boot in the spring. Clear water slips around its heel. Even here, something finds a way through.
Suggested line: Someone has thrown a boot in the spring. The water has gone politely round it.
Why: Restores the dry running gag (the water going politely round the boot) and drops the platitude.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You recall the first words of every Gourmand recipe: first, water. Someone has added 'and salt' here. Twice.
Suggested line: Every Gourmand recipe still begins with the same two words: first, water. Somebody has added 'and salt' here. Twice.
Why: Drops the 'You recall' frame; the player cannot recall a recipe, the narration can state it.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: A well with opinions. I'll take a bottle's worth.
Suggested line: A well with opinions. Fine. I'm keeping the bottle.
Why: Restores the Wanderer's version (story bible): 'Fine.' is his undercut, and 'keeping' lands the joke.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You hear the scale model split. The table cracks beneath it, and the sound travels through the castle walls.
Suggested line: The scale model cracks in half. Then the table cracks. Then, with the sound of a very large drawer being pulled from a very large cabinet, the castle walls begin to come down.
Why: Restores the precise, filing-cabinet image of Primm's castle falling; the current 'You hear' line is flat.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: In {showcase}, a painted door falls flat. You see a citizen step through onto the street beyond.
Suggested line: In {showcase}, a painted door falls flat, and a very surprised citizen steps through it onto a very real street.
Why: Restores painted door versus real street (the facade theme) and drops 'You see'.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You see Fig Sly among the people emerging from the Crease. He carries his stock with him.
Suggested line: Fig Sly comes up out of the Crease already selling something, to somebody, for some reason. Nobody stops him.
Why: Narration about him, not his line: restores the story bible beat ('already selling something') over a flat description.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You watch the four Paths gather around their leaders, carrying what they have saved from the past ten years.
Suggested line: The Beefcakes are late. The Necrocrats have brought a form. The Gourmands are overdressed. The Refusemancers smell, faintly, of compost.
Why: Restores the four Paths arriving in character (story bible beat 7); the current line is generic.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You see hands marked by iron, flour, ink and soil reach across the space between the four groups.
Suggested line: Muscle and stoves, records and soil: each was good alone. Together they ran a kingdom, argued about it every day, and it worked.
Why: Restores the game's thesis, which sets up 'The point was the argument' in the next box.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You read the changes beneath it: MAY crossed out for SHOULD, then WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. Four hands have left their marks.
Suggested line: Somebody has crossed out MAY and written SHOULD. Somebody else has crossed out SHOULD and written WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. A pigeon sits on the full stop.
Why: Shows the four hands arguing on the wall instead of summarising it; the pigeon is the quiet last turn.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: For everyone who waited to be heard.
Suggested line: In memory of Form 27-B, Form 27-C and Form 27-B
Why: Credits may carry a joke: restores the forms callback over a generic dedication.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: For everyone learning to choose again.
Suggested line: No hats were harmed. Several were enlarged.
Why: Restores the regulation-hat callback; the credits had two near-identical dedications in a row.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Effective line: Thank you, dear. I have written it down, though that hardly seems enough.
Suggested line: I have filed a Form of Gratitude, dear. It was approved on the first attempt. Irregular.
Why: Pays off Agnes's 'Irregular.' gag and her denied appeals; the next box ('going to cry') stays sincere.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: the Pathwork Throne
Suggested line: The Pathwork Throne
Why: Title case, like every other beat title; the lower-case 'the' is a slip from the earlier pass.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Effective line: You see Maren make her way through the crowd. She stops in front of you, flour still on her sleeve.
Suggested line: Maren pushes through the crowd, tortoise-slow, and stops in front of you. There is flour on her sleeve.
Why: Keeps the flour, drops 'You see', and lets her slowness show how hard she is pushing.

Speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
Effective line: He designs good drains. The guard stays here while he works.
Suggested line: He designs very good drains, it turns out. Do not tell him I said so.
Why: Current line has the guard call himself 'the guard'; this one also quietly withholds the praise Primm wants.

Speaker: Isla Brannoch
Effective line: You're the one who knocked the castle over? Dad says hi. Dad says a lot, actually. Thank you.
Suggested line: You're the one who knocked the castle over? Dad says thank you. That's what the 'Hm' meant. Thank you from me, too.
Why: 'Dad says a lot' contradicts the man who just said 'Hm.'; this reads his 'Hm' instead, warmly.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: In the Capital's square, you watch the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands. Several people cry.
Suggested line: In the Capital's square, the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands. Nobody trips. Several people cry.
Why: Drops 'you watch' and restores 'Nobody trips.', the small turn that keeps the still from being solemn.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Above you, four banners share one crowded pole.
Suggested line: Four banners fly from the same pole. It is a little crowded, and nobody minds.
Why: Restores 'and nobody minds', which says the whole ending in five words.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: At the crowd's edge, you see a hooded traveler smile, leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.
Suggested line: At the edge of the crowd, a hooded traveler smiles, leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.
Why: Drops 'you see'; the traveler is the player, so narrating that 'you see' him reads oddly.
